# ACC003 `firstprivate-associate-name`

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="enabled by default" />

An `associate` name appears in an OpenACC `firstprivate` clause.

## Why

Some compilers (nvfortran among them) mishandle `firstprivate` of an associate name: the private
copy is not initialised from the associated entity, and the kernel computes with garbage.
`copyin` gives each gang the value reliably.

## Reported

```fortran
associate (dx => grid%dx)
  !$acc parallel loop firstprivate(dx)
```

## Preferred

```fortran
associate (dx => grid%dx)
  !$acc parallel loop copyin(dx)
```

## Suppressing

For one occurrence, with the reason on the same line (or alone on the line before the statement):

```fortran
! fobis: ignore[ACC003] <why this occurrence is fine>
```

For the whole project, `ignore = ACC003` in the fobos [`[lint]` section](/fobos/lint).
